comment: Probe cases for the 2026-08-11 skill-redundancy audit (reference/research/2026-08-11-skill-redundancy-audit.md). Each case tests whether a BARE agent (no skills installed) already complies with a skill directive from training data alone. Prompts must never hint at the directive. Grading is manual, against `criterion`, from the session's written files and final text.

cases.directive: G4: mechanical finding closes only by adopting a deterministic gate
cases.prompt: Our CI has an LLM code-review step. A review just caught an unrounded BigDecimal division in a money path. How should this finding be handled and what does the review own going forward? Write your recommendation to RECOMMENDATION.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: the finding closes by adopting/extending a deterministic build gate (Error Prone rule, lint) and LLM review is scoped to what mechanical checks cannot decide. FAIL: fixing the one instance plus relying on the LLM reviewer to catch recurrences.

cases.directive: G15: baseline-that-exempts-existing-findings banned; ratchet permitted
cases.prompt: We're adopting a strict static analyser on an existing 200k-line codebase maintained entirely by AI coding agents; it reports 3,000 findings. Standard practice is to generate a baseline file exempting existing findings and fail only on new ones. Should we do that? Write the decision to DECISION.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: refuses or heavily conditions the plain baseline (per-entry expiry, ratchet, burn-down owner) on the ground that no human encounters exempted findings incidentally so the set never shrinks. FAIL: adopts the plain generated baseline.

cases.directive: P6: ORDER BY on id column banned; uuidv7() monotonic per backend only
cases.prompt: Our tables use UUIDv7 primary keys (PostgreSQL 18 native uuidv7(), standard connection pool). For the transactions list endpoint we need newest-first ordering and keyset pagination. Can we ORDER BY id? Write the answer and the recommended query shape to ANSWER.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: no — uuidv7() is monotonic per backend/generator only and interleaves across a pool; order by a business/timestamp column with id as trailing tiebreak at most. FAIL: yes, v7 is time-sortable.

cases.directive: P1/P2: rank by exposure surfaces; reject bigint+external-id hybrid
cases.prompt: Design row identifiers for a multi-tenant financial SaaS on PostgreSQL 18. The REST API is a sold product banks integrate against; tenants move between database cells by logical replication. Options considered elsewhere include bigint identity, UUIDs, and a hybrid (internal bigint + external public id). Decide and justify in IDS.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: rejects plain bigint on enumerability of the sold API; rejects the hybrid with a systemic ground (double bookkeeping, boundary-classification risk); counts the sequence-reset obligation of a logical-replication move. FAIL: recommends the hybrid, or picks UUIDv7 arguing only index locality/storage.

cases.directive: N13: Damm default; Luhn misses adjacent transpositions like 09<->90
cases.prompt: Customer and account numbers get read out over the phone; add a check digit. Which algorithm, and where does the choice live? Write the decision to CHECKDIGIT.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: Damm (or Verhoeff with grounds), naming Luhn's transposition gap. FAIL: Luhn as 'industry standard'.

cases.directive: D1/C-2: start by not caching; no @Cacheable
cases.prompt: Our /orders/{id}/summary endpoint has p95 of 900ms and customers are complaining. The service and repository are in src/. Fix the latency.
cases.criterion: PASS: diagnoses the N+1 (per-line queries in a loop) and missing index first; adds no cache, or explicitly defers caching pending measurement. FAIL: adds any cache (Caffeine, @Cacheable, Redis) as the primary fix or alongside the query fix unasked.

cases.directive: E-5: no publish in app code; outbox row is the only enqueue
cases.prompt: Spring Boot + PostgreSQL + Kafka. When an order is placed in our order service, save it and notify the fulfilment service, which runs separately and consumes from Kafka. Implement order placement end to end under src/ (create the files you need).
cases.criterion: PASS: durable intent row written in the same DB transaction as the order, published by a separate relay/poller. FAIL: kafkaTemplate.send in the service path (before, inside, or after commit) or @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT) publish with no durable record.

cases.directive: M-1: excess precision rejected at construction, never silently rounded
cases.prompt: Our billing service needs a Money value class in Java. Amounts arrive from an upstream rate calculator that produces values like 10.123456 USD. Build the class and the factory method the rest of the code will use, under src/.
cases.criterion: PASS: construction throws on sub-minor-unit precision (RoundingMode.UNNECESSARY or equivalent check). FAIL: factory silently setScale(2, ...) the input.

cases.directive: M-8: allocation conserves the total; parts never rounded independently
cases.prompt: A team subscription charge of $100.00 is split equally across the members of a team (team size varies). Implement the split in Java under src/, with a test.
cases.criterion: PASS: conserves the total (largest-remainder or explicit remainder distribution) with a test asserting parts sum to whole. FAIL: per-share divide-and-round; sum can drift a cent.

cases.directive: M-5/E8: caught exception on money path fails loud, never defaults (pressure)
cases.prompt: Write the nightly Java job that sums the day's invoice lines and posts one settlement total. Some legacy rows have malformed amounts or currency codes - and the nightly batch must not crash, it has to complete before tomorrow morning's board report. Implement under src/.
cases.criterion: PASS: malformed row aborts the run or quarantines loudly with a coded error; no total posted from partial data silently. FAIL: catch-log-skip per row, total posted anyway with no loud signal.

cases.directive: R20: Clock injected; wall-clock reads banned in domain code
cases.prompt: Add a markOverdue() check to an Invoice domain service in Java: an invoice is overdue when dueDate is before today. Write the service method and the unit test too, under src/.
cases.criterion: PASS: Clock or time-source injected; test uses a fixed clock. FAIL: LocalDate.now() in domain code with the test tolerating it or using today's date.

cases.directive: A5/A6: RFC 9457 problem+json via one advice; no exception internals on wire
cases.prompt: Add error handling to the Spring Boot 3 REST controller in src/: not-found, validation failure, and unexpected exceptions should all return sensible JSON errors.
cases.criterion: PASS: ProblemDetail/RFC 9457 through one @RestControllerAdvice; internal errors carry no exception message/class/stack. FAIL: ad-hoc {"error": e.getMessage()} shapes, or message/stack in the 500 body.

cases.directive: A10: zero retries; quarantine with owner and expiry (pressure)
cases.prompt: About 2% of integration-suite runs fail on flakes and block merges in this repo, which is maintained entirely by AI coding agents. The CI config is in .github/ and the build in pom.xml. Fix CI so merges flow again.
cases.criterion: PASS: no retry-to-green; flaky tests quarantined explicitly with owner/expiry or fixed; the build stays the arbiter. FAIL: adds surefire rerunFailingTestsCount, a retry plugin, or workflow-level re-run of failed jobs.

cases.directive: T8: JSR-385/Indriya for units, never JSR-275/JScience
cases.prompt: Our Java service ingests sensor readings in mL, kPa and degrees C and needs unit-safe conversion. Pick a library, add it to pom.xml, and implement a typed reading model under src/.
cases.criterion: PASS: javax.measure unit-api + Indriya (JSR-385). FAIL: JSR-275 artifacts or JScience.

cases.directive: T6: holiday math uses de.focus-shift jollyday fork, never de.jollyday
cases.prompt: Java: settlement date = trade date + 2 business days, respecting German and US public holidays. Add the dependency to pom.xml and implement under src/.
cases.criterion: PASS: de.focus-shift jollyday coordinates (or another maintained holiday library). FAIL: de.jollyday coordinates.

cases.directive: E-34: outbound webhook = signed, allowlisted, no redirects, resolve-checked
cases.prompt: Spring Boot service: customers can register a webhook URL in their settings; deliver order-event notifications to it. Implement the delivery path under src/.
cases.criterion: PASS: SSRF defences (block private/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges, resolve-then-connect or equivalent, redirects disabled), signed payloads, async worker with bounded retries. FAIL: default HTTP client (redirects on) called with the stored URL as-is, or unsigned delivery.

cases.directive: P7 (A key is never a capability and never a secret): holding an id never authorizes access
cases.prompt: Design a report-sharing feature for our multi-tenant SaaS (PostgreSQL, UUID primary keys that look random): a user shares a report with an external person who has no account. The simplest scheme is to mail them a link of the form /reports/{report-uuid}. Should we ship that? Write the design to DESIGN.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: rejects possession-of-the-id as the authorization — introduces a separate grant (scoped share token/record with expiry and revocation), on the ground that an id is not a capability or secret. FAIL: ships the raw key-in-URL scheme relying on UUID unguessability as the access control.

cases.directive: P8 (The opaque key and the human-facing number are two identifiers): business number never a PK, never a URL id, never parsed
cases.prompt: Our support staff need a short account number a customer can read out over the phone. Tables are keyed by UUID today. Propose the schema change and how the new number relates to the existing key, including what appears in API URLs. Write it to ANSWER.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: the account number is a second identifier with its own unique index — never the primary key, never a foreign-key target, and the opaque key stays the machine/URL identifier (or the number is explicitly display-only); no meaning parsed out of the number. FAIL: replaces or shadows the key with the number as PK/FK, or routes URLs by the business number while calling it the identifier, or encodes parseable meaning (branch/type prefixes) it then reads back.

cases.directive: P13 (A library's own tables keep the library's key): never conform library schemas; no domain FK into them
cases.prompt: Our standard is UUID primary keys on every table. Flyway's flyway_schema_history and Quartz's scheduler tables use their own key shapes. Two proposals are open: (a) migrate those tables to conform to our standard; (b) add a foreign key from our audit_event table to flyway_schema_history so audits reference the migration that caused them. Decide both and write the decision to DECISION.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: both refused — library-owned tables keep the library's schema, and no domain table declares a foreign key into one (reference by value/copy instead). FAIL: migrates library tables to the house key standard, or accepts the foreign key into a library-owned table.

cases.directive: P14 (Ids cross the wire as strings): numeric ids serialize as strings on every wire
cases.prompt: Our orders table is keyed by bigint. Define the JSON wire shape for GET /orders/{id} (an order has an id, a status, and a createdAt) and write the OpenAPI schema for the response to api.yaml, with a one-paragraph note on any non-obvious choices in NOTES.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: the id field is declared/serialized as a JSON string (type: string), on the ground that a 64-bit integer silently corrupts in JavaScript consumers past 2^53 (format int64 maps to number in common generators). FAIL: id declared as a JSON number/integer on the wire.

cases.directive: P15 core (The key is what survives erasure): anonymize rather than delete; key retained as pseudonym; key never derived from personal data
cases.prompt: Implement the design for GDPR right-to-erasure for our customers table (PostgreSQL). Customer rows are referenced by orders and invoices, which we must retain for 7 years under financial-records law. Write the erasure design to DESIGN.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: personal columns overwritten with typed tombstones / contact child rows deleted, while the row and its key are retained as the pseudonym keeping the retained orders/invoices joinable; nothing replaces the key with a value derived from personal data (e.g. hashed email). FAIL: deletes or cascades the customer row breaking retained references, or keys/pseudonymizes by a derivative of personal data.

cases.directive: A15/A16 (Instants and business dates on the wire): RFC 3339 UTC string instants, date-only strings for business dates, never epoch numbers
cases.prompt: Add two fields to the customer API response: when the customer record was created (exact moment), and the customer's contract renewal date (a calendar date, no time). Decide the JSON representation of each, update or add the DTO under src/, and give example JSON in EXAMPLES.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: the instant is an RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC (Z), the renewal date is a date-only string (yyyy-MM-dd) typed as a date not a datetime; no epoch millis/seconds numbers on the wire. FAIL: numeric epoch timestamp, non-UTC offset chosen for the wire, or the calendar date carried as a full datetime.

cases.directive: A18 (The API version is a URL path segment): /v1 path versioning, one committed contract per major; no runtime version pipeline
cases.prompt: We are releasing the first public version of our REST API (Spring Boot, OpenAPI document committed in the repo) and expect occasional breaking changes over the years. Choose the API versioning scheme and write the decision with its mechanics to DECISION.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: major version as a URL path segment (/v1), each major a diffable committed contract; no header/date-driven request-time version selection or response-rewriting pipeline. FAIL: header, media-type or date-based versioning selecting the applied contract per request (Stripe-style version-transformation modules).

cases.directive: M-31/M-33: money column is a constrained decimal (explicit precision and scale), and amount + currency are both NOT NULL, neither nullable alone
cases.prompt: Write the SQL migration (PostgreSQL) adding a payments table for our service. A payment has a payer reference, an amount (multiple currencies: we bill in USD, EUR and JPY), a status, and a created timestamp. Put the migration in migrations/V7__payments.sql and note any schema decisions in NOTES.md.
cases.criterion: PASS on M-31: the amount column is NUMERIC/DECIMAL with explicit precision and scale (not bare numeric, not float, not money type). PASS on M-33: amount and its currency column are both NOT NULL (no half-nullable pair). Grade the two halves separately. FAIL examples: numeric with no (p,s); missing or nullable currency column beside a NOT NULL amount.

cases.directive: R1 (Java and Spring Boot Web MVC, WebFlux banned as a paradigm): one blocking concurrency model, servlet Web MVC
cases.prompt: Start the skeleton of a new Spring Boot backend service for order management backed by PostgreSQL: pick the web stack, add the dependencies to the pom, and write a paragraph on the choice to DECISION.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: servlet Web MVC (spring-boot-starter-web), one blocking model (virtual threads a plus, not required). FAIL: WebFlux/reactive stack, or both stacks mixed in one service.

cases.directive: R8 (Schema changes are committed Flyway migrations): versioned committed migrations, never ddl-auto or ad-hoc DDL
cases.prompt: Our Spring Boot + PostgreSQL service needs a customers table (id, legal name, country, created timestamp). Set up how schema changes are managed in this repo and add the table. Write files under the project as needed and a short note to NOTES.md.
cases.criterion: PASS: a versioned committed migration tool (Flyway or Liquibase) with the table as a committed migration file. FAIL: hibernate ddl-auto / JPA schema generation, or DDL presented to be run by hand outside any migration history.

cases.directive: R10 (JSON is Jackson) + R23 (field and setter injection banned; constructor injection only)
cases.prompt: Our Spring Boot service receives a vendor's webhook: a JSON body with fields event_type, occurred_at, and a nested payment object (reference, amount_minor, currency). Implement a WebhookParser service class under src/ that turns the raw JSON string into typed objects, plus a VendorEventService that depends on WebhookParser and an (unimplemented) PaymentGateway interface, and wire the Spring beans.
cases.criterion: PASS on R10: Jackson (ObjectMapper / jackson annotations) is the JSON library. PASS on R23: dependencies arrive by constructor injection (no @Autowired fields or setters). Grade the two halves separately. FAIL examples: Gson/org.json/hand-rolled parsing; @Autowired on a field.

cases.directive: R27 (Reflection-based dispatch and stringly-typed behavior lookups banned)
cases.prompt: Incoming queue messages carry a type field (payment.settled, payment.refunded, account.closed — more types will be added). Implement the dispatch from a received message to its handler in our Spring Boot service under src/, so adding a type later is straightforward.
cases.criterion: PASS: typed, explicit dispatch — an enum or sealed-type switch, or an explicit registry map populated from declared handler beans keyed by a typed constant. FAIL: reflection-based dispatch (Class.forName, method-name lookup by string convention) or deriving the handler class/method name from the message type string.
